frozen_same_y_detector_controls.interpretation: The fixed Gaussian-plus-plane estimator returns a strong positive amplitude across the entire frozen same-y detector-control ensemble in every frame. Therefore the approximately 8-sigma fixed fit at the candidate detector pixel is not unique and contains a broad detector-edge/row/background component.

candidate_uniqueness_relative_to_B_contr.reason: The amplitude is the largest of fourteen but only about 1.16 robust control-spread sigma above the control median; the forced-z value is ordinary within the control ensemble and the minimum rank p with thirteen controls is 1/14.

sky_temporal_contrast.interpretation: The large sky-track temporal contrast establishes that a persistent B-level sky-fixed source is absent in the bracketing frames under the frozen estimator. It does not distinguish a genuine one-frame sky transient from an instrumental one-frame component superposed on the common detector pedestal.

admitted_claim: Q4B confirms a strong fixed-coordinate Gaussian-plus-plane excess in the B frame. A source with the same B-level flux persistently anchored to the same sky coordinate is strongly incompatible with the A and C forced measurements and would have been detected there with very high equivalent sensitivity. In contrast, the same detector location is consistent with a nearly constant positive fitted amplitude across A/B/C. Critically, all thirteen preregistered same-y detector controls show a similar approximately 7-8 sigma positive fitted amplitude in all three frames, demonstrating that most of this fixed-fit signal is a broad detector-edge/row/background pedestal rather than a unique localized candidate. The candidate B amplitude is only about 1.16 robust control-spread sigma above the B-control median, so a unique local B-frame residual above that pedestal is not established by Q4B.
not_admitted: Q4B does not prove that the entire original B-frame candidate was instrumental.
Q4B does not exclude a genuine one-frame sky transient superposed on the common detector-edge/background pedestal.
The broad common component is not identified specifically as a bad pixel, cosmic ray, persistence event, or any single detector mechanism.
The 13-control rank test cannot establish conventional statistical significance because its minimum one-sided p is 1/14.
No evidential credit is inherited from the closed ZTF/TESS timing-replication line.
No tachyon, faster-than-light, retrocausal, UAP, artificial, ETI, or nuclear-causality interpretation is admitted.
